title: TN SB0677: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, relative to artificial intelligence.

obligations: The department shall provide at least one professional development course for teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom, made available at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve, and that may be used to earn professional development points (Section 1(a)).
The course content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Section 1(a)).

By August 1, 2028, or within two years of becoming licensed as a teacher in this state, whichever is later, teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one professional development course approved by the department that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom (Section 1(b)).

Each LEA and public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Section 1(b)).

What it does

The department of education must provide at least one asynchronous professional development course on using artificial intelligence in the classroom, at no cost, for teachers in grades six through twelve, and the course may earn professional development points. Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one department approved artificial intelligence course by August 1, 2028, or within two years of licensure, whichever is later. Each LEA and public charter school must approve professional development points for completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training.

Who it applies to

  • the department of education
  • teachers in grades six through twelve
  • each LEA
  • each public charter school

Effective date

upon becoming a law (Section 2)

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • The department shall provide at least one professional development course for teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom, made available at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve, and that may be used to earn professional development points (Section 1(a)).
  • The course content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Section 1(a)).
  • By August 1, 2028, or within two years of becoming licensed as a teacher in this state, whichever is later, teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one professional development course approved by the department that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom (Section 1(b)).
  • Each LEA and public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Section 1(b)).

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • An LEA or public charter school must approve professional development points for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Section 1(b)).
  • Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete the required artificial intelligence course by the deadline, which may affect staffing and training schedules in schools (Section 1(b)).
  • The department must ensure the course content is created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as computer science or a science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Section 1(a)).
  • The statute does not impose direct requirements on private organisations that deploy artificial intelligence; its requirements fall on the department, teachers, LEAs, and public charter schools (Section 1).

Compliance steps

  • The department must develop or procure at least one asynchronous professional development course on artificial intelligence for classroom use, at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve, with content created by an entity with experience in computer science or a science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Section 1(a)).
  • Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one department approved artificial intelligence course by August 1, 2028, or within two years of licensure, whichever is later (Section 1(b)).
  • Each LEA and public charter school must approve professional development points for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training under state board of education licensure policies and rules (Section 1(b)).

 Substituted for: House Bill No. 545

 By Cochran, Cepicky, Hardaway

AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, relative to artificial intelligence.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 2, is amended by adding
the following as a new section:

 (a) The department shall provide at least one (1) professional development course for
 teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the
 classroom; that is made available, at no cost, to teachers in grades six through twelve (6-12);
 and that may be used by teachers to earn professional development points. The course
 content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as
 computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics {STEM)
 field.

 (b) By August 1, 2028, or within two (2) years of becoming licensed as a teacher in
 this state, whichever is later, teachers in grades six through twelve (6-12) must complete at
 least one ( 1) professional development course approved by the department that provides
 asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom. Each LEA and
 public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state
 board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at
 least one (1) department-approved artificial intelligence training.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
  SENATE BILL NO. 677
